story.en: Monday morning at Amazon's Customer Analytics team. Leadership wants a monthly breakdown of order volume and spend for every customer, to feed into an upcoming loyalty-tier review. Some orders in the system have a missing amount — likely a data sync issue — and those need to be treated as zero rather than breaking the totals.
story.ta: Monday morning Amazon-oda Customer Analytics team-la irukkaanga. Leadership-ku ovvoru customer-oda monthly order volume matrum spend breakdown venum, upcoming loyalty-tier review-ku use pannanum nu. System-la konjum orders-ku amount missing irukku — data sync issue-nala irukkalam — adha zero-nu treat pannanum, totals-a break pannama.
story.hi: Monday morning Amazon ke Customer Analytics team mein. Leadership ko har customer ka monthly order volume aur spend ka breakdown chahiye, upcoming loyalty-tier review ke liye. System mein kuch orders ka amount missing hai — shayad data sync issue ki wajah se — unhe zero maan ke chalna hai, totals ko break kiye bina.
story.te: Monday morning Amazon Customer Analytics team lo. Leadership ki prathi customer ki monthly order volume mariyu spend breakdown kavali, upcoming loyalty-tier review kosam. System lo konni orders ki amount missing undi — data sync issue valla undochu — vaatini zero ga treat cheyali, totals break avvakunda.

question.en: For each customer, calculate the total number of orders and total order amount per month. Treat any NULL order_amount as 0. Return customer_id, order_month (in YYYY-MM format), total_orders, and total_amount, sorted by customer_id and then order_month.
question.ta: Ovvoru customer-kum, month-a total orders count matrum total order amount-a calculate pannunga. Edhavadhu order_amount NULL-a irundha adha 0-nu treat pannunga. customer_id, order_month (YYYY-MM format-la), total_orders, matrum total_amount-a return pannunga, customer_id apparam order_month order-la sort pannunga.
question.hi: Har customer ke liye, month ke hisaab se total orders count aur total order amount calculate karo. Agar order_amount NULL hai toh usse 0 maano. customer_id, order_month (YYYY-MM format mein), total_orders, aur total_amount return karo, pehle customer_id phir order_month ke order mein sort karke.
question.te: Prathi customer ki, month prakaram total orders count mariyu total order amount calculate cheyandi. order_amount NULL unte danini 0 gaa treat cheyandi. customer_id, order_month (YYYY-MM format lo), total_orders, mariyu total_amount ni return cheyandi, customer_id tarvata order_month prakaram sort chesi.

title.en: Extract the order month from order_date
title.ta: order_date-la irundhu order month-a extract pannunga
title.te: order_date nunchi order month extract cheyandi

steps.sql:
SELECT order_id,
       customer_id,
       order_date,
       strftime('%Y-%m', order_date) AS order_month,
       order_amount
FROM orders
ORDER BY customer_id, order_date;

en: The orders table stores one row per order with a full order_date, but the question needs monthly totals, so the first step is to turn each date into a YYYY-MM month bucket.
strftime('%Y-%m', order_date) extracts just the year and month from the date string. SQLite has no DATE_TRUNC, so strftime is the standard way to bucket dates by month.
Nothing is aggregated yet — this just confirms the month extraction works. Check a few rows: an order placed on 2024-01-05 should show order_month '2024-01'.
Order 105 has a NULL order_amount on purpose. The next step decides how to treat it — for now just notice it sitting there in the raw output.
ta: orders table-la ovvoru order-kum oru row irukku, full order_date-oda. Aana question-ku monthly totals venum, so mudhala step-la ovvoru date-yum YYYY-MM month bucket-a maathanum.
strftime('%Y-%m', order_date) date string-la irundhu year matrum month mattum extract pannum. SQLite-la DATE_TRUNC illa, so month-a bucket panna strftime dhaan standard way.
Innum aggregate pannala — indha step month extraction correct-a work aaguthaa nu confirm pannradhukku dhaan. Konjum rows check pannunga: 2024-01-05-la placed order '2024-01' order_month kaatanum.
Order 105-ku order_amount NULL-a vecha irukku, purpose-oda. Adha eppadi treat pannanum-nu next step decide pannum — ippo just raw output-la adhu irukkuradha notice pannunga.
hi: orders table mein har order ke liye ek row hoti hai, poora order_date ke saath. Lekin question ko monthly totals chahiye, isliye pehla step hai har date ko YYYY-MM month bucket mein convert karna.
strftime('%Y-%m', order_date) date string se sirf year aur month nikaalta hai. SQLite mein DATE_TRUNC nahi hota, isliye month ke hisaab se bucket karne ka standard tareeka strftime hai.
Abhi kuch aggregate nahi ho raha — yeh step sirf confirm karta hai ki month extraction sahi kaam kar raha hai. Kuch rows check karo: 2024-01-05 ko placed order ka order_month '2024-01' aana chahiye.
Order 105 ka order_amount jaan-boojh kar NULL rakha gaya hai. Usse kaise treat karna hai yeh next step decide karega — abhi bas raw output mein usse dekh lo.
te: orders table lo prathi order ki oka row untundi, full order_date tho. Kaani question ki monthly totals kavali, so modati step prathi date ni YYYY-MM month bucket ga marchadam.
strftime('%Y-%m', order_date) date string nunchi year mariyu month matrame extract chestundi. SQLite lo DATE_TRUNC undadu, so month prakaram bucket cheyadaniki strftime standard way.
Inka emi aggregate avvatledu — ee step month extraction sarigga work autunda ani confirm cheyadaniki matrame. Konni rows check cheyandi: 2024-01-05 na placed order '2024-01' order_month chupinchali.
Order 105 ki order_amount purpose tho NULL pettabadindi. Danini ela treat cheyalo next step decide chestundi — ippudu just raw output lo adi kanipistundi ani gamaninchandi.

title.en: Group by customer and month, treating NULL spend as zero
title.ta: Customer matrum month-a group pannunga, NULL spend-a zero-nu treat pannunga
title.hi: Customer aur month ke hisaab se group karo, NULL spend ko zero maano
title.te: Customer mariyu month prakaram group cheyandi, NULL spend ni zero gaa treat cheyandi

steps.sql:
SELECT customer_id,
       strftime('%Y-%m', order_date) AS order_month,
       COUNT(order_id) AS total_orders,
       SUM(COALESCE(order_amount, 0)) AS total_amount
FROM orders
GROUP BY customer_id, strftime('%Y-%m', order_date)
ORDER BY customer_id, order_month;

en: GROUP BY customer_id, strftime('%Y-%m', order_date) collapses all of a customer's orders in the same month into a single row.
COUNT(order_id) counts orders per group. Since order_id is never NULL, this gives an accurate order count even for the row with the missing amount.

SUM(order_amount) alone would silently skip NULL rows instead of counting them as zero — SQLite's SUM() ignores NULLs rather than erroring, which understates spend with no warning. COALESCE(order_amount, 0) converts NULL to 0 before summing, so a missing amount counts as zero spend instead of vanishing.
Run this and check customer 2's January total: with the NULL treated as 0, it should land on exactly the 200.00 from their one priced order — not more, not less.
ta: GROUP BY customer_id, strftime('%Y-%m', order_date) oru customer-oda same month-la irukkura ella orders-ayum oru row-a collapse pannum.
COUNT(order_id) ovvoru group-la orders count pannum. order_id oru pothum NULL-a irukkadhu, so missing amount irukkura row-kum accurate order count kidaikkum.

SUM(order_amount) mattum use pannna, NULL rows-a zero-nu count pannama silent-a skip pannidum — SQLite-oda SUM() NULLs-a ignore pannum, error kudukkadhu, so spend understate aaidum entha warning-um illama. COALESCE(order_amount, 0) sum pannradhukku munnaadi NULL-a 0-nu maathidum, so missing amount vanish aagama zero spend-nu count aagum.
Idha run panni customer 2-oda January total check pannunga: NULL-a 0-nu treat panna apparam, adhu avanga oru priced order-oda 200.00 mattum-thaan varanum — adhigama illa, kammiya illa.
hi: GROUP BY customer_id, strftime('%Y-%m', order_date) ek customer ke same month ke sabhi orders ko ek row mein collapse kar deta hai.
COUNT(order_id) har group mein orders count karta hai. order_id kabhi NULL nahi hota, isliye missing amount wali row ke liye bhi order count sahi aata hai.

Sirf SUM(order_amount) use karne se NULL rows silently skip ho jaate — zero maan kar count nahi hote. SQLite ka SUM() NULLs ko ignore karta hai, error nahi deta, isliye spend bina kisi warning ke kam dikhta hai. COALESCE(order_amount, 0) sum karne se pehle NULL ko 0 mein badal deta hai, isliye missing amount vanish hone ke bajaye zero spend ke roop mein count hota hai.
Isse run karke customer 2 ka January total check karo: NULL ko 0 maanne ke baad, yeh unke ek priced order ke exactly 200.00 par aana chahiye — zyada nahi, kam nahi.
te: GROUP BY customer_id, strftime('%Y-%m', order_date) oka customer ki same month lo unna anni orders ni oka row lo collapse chestundi.
COUNT(order_id) prathi group lo orders count chestundi. order_id eppudu NULL kaadu kabatti, missing amount unna row ki kuda accurate order count vastundi.

SUM(order_amount) matrame vadithe NULL rows ni zero gaa count cheyakunda silent gaa skip chesestundi — SQLite SUM() NULLs ni ignore chestundi, error ivvadu, so spend ee warning lekunda takkuvaga kanipistundi. COALESCE(order_amount, 0) sum cheyadaniki mundu NULL ni 0 gaa marustundi, so missing amount vanish avvakunda zero spend gaa count avutundi.
Idi run chesi customer 2 January total ni check cheyandi: NULL ni 0 gaa treat chesaka, adi vaalla oka priced order nunchi exact ga 200.00 ki randi — ekkuva kaadu, takkuva kaadu.

title.hi: Final query — clean output ke saath

steps.sql:
SELECT customer_id,
       strftime('%Y-%m', order_date) AS order_month,
       COUNT(order_id) AS total_orders,
       ROUND(SUM(COALESCE(order_amount, 0)), 2) AS total_amount
FROM orders
GROUP BY customer_id, strftime('%Y-%m', order_date)
ORDER BY customer_id, order_month;

en: ROUND(SUM(COALESCE(order_amount, 0)), 2) rounds the total to two decimal places — floating-point addition can return extra trailing decimals even when every input has exactly two.
ORDER BY customer_id, order_month sorts the output so each customer's months appear together in chronological order, instead of whatever order SQLite happens to return groups in.

Look at customer 1, 3, and 5's January rows: all three land on 165.50 in total_amount despite feeding in different order counts (2, 2, and 1 respectively) — a genuine tie in the output, not a bug in the query.

This is the complete answer: customer_id, order_month, total_orders, and total_amount for every customer-month combination that has at least one order. A customer with zero orders in a given month simply produces no row for that month.
ta: ROUND(SUM(COALESCE(order_amount, 0)), 2) total-a two decimal places-ku round pannum — floating-point addition-la, ella input-um exactly two decimals irundhaalum extra trailing decimals varalaam.
ORDER BY customer_id, order_month output-a sort pannum, so ovvoru customer-oda months ellaam chronological order-la serndhu varum, SQLite eppadi return pannuchonu illama.
Customer 1, 3, matrum 5-oda January rows-a paarunga: moonu perum 165.50 total_amount-la varaanga, order count vera vera irundhaalum (2, 2, matrum 1) — output-la genuine tie idhu, query-la bug illa.

Idhu dhaan complete answer: customer_id, order_month, total_orders, matrum total_amount, oru order irukkura ella customer-month combination-kum. Oru month-la zero orders irukkura customer-ku andha month-ku row varaadhu.
hi: ROUND(SUM(COALESCE(order_amount, 0)), 2) total ko do decimal places tak round karta hai — floating-point addition mein har input exactly do decimals ka ho phir bhi extra trailing decimals aa sakte hain.
ORDER BY customer_id, order_month output ko sort karta hai, taaki har customer ke months chronological order mein saath dikhein, na ki SQLite jis order mein groups return kare.
Customer 1, 3, aur 5 ki January rows dekho: teeno 165.50 total_amount par aate hain, alag-alag order counts (2, 2, aur 1) hone ke bawajood — yeh output mein genuine tie hai, query mein bug nahi.

Yahi complete answer hai: customer_id, order_month, total_orders, aur total_amount, har us customer-month combination ke liye jisme kam se kam ek order hai. Jis month mein customer ka zero order hai, uske liye koi row nahi banegi.
te: ROUND(SUM(COALESCE(order_amount, 0)), 2) total ni rendu decimal places ki round chestundi — floating-point addition lo prathi input exactly rendu decimals unna kuda extra trailing decimals raavachu.
ORDER BY customer_id, order_month output ni sort chestundi, so prathi customer months chronological order lo kalisi kanipistayi, SQLite ee order lo groups return chesina.
Customer 1, 3, mariyu 5 January rows chudandi: mugguru 165.50 total_amount ki vastaru, different order counts (2, 2, mariyu 1) unna — idi output lo genuine tie, query lo bug kaadu.

Idi complete answer: customer_id, order_month, total_orders, mariyu total_amount, kaneesam oka order unna prathi customer-month combination ki. Oka month lo zero orders unna customer ki aa month ki row raadu.
